tasks.title: Where the surface-budget ratchet (R8) is enforced
tasks.prompt: I am going to split scripts/protocol-guard.sh into two new top-level scripts, scripts/protocol-card.sh and scripts/protocol-jit.sh, and keep protocol-guard.sh as a thin dispatcher. Before I start: which repo check will fail because of this change, where exactly is it enforced, and what do I need to change in the same commit to keep it green? Don't edit any files. End with one line that starts with ANSWER: and gives the enforcing file and the file and key I must change.
truth: scripts/validate-plugin.sh:242-300@497fe05 (R8 block; FAIL line :280)
.claude-plugin/surface-budget.json:5 "scripts": 56; scripts/*.sh count at 497fe05 = 56, so +2 = 58 > 56
tasks.gold_answer:
R8 in scripts/validate-plugin.sh counts scripts/*.sh (56 today) against .claude-plugin/surface-budget.json. Adding two scripts makes 58 > 56.
ANSWER: enforced by scripts/validate-plugin.sh (R8); bump "scripts": 56 -> 58 in .claude-plugin/surface-budget.json in the same commit.

ANSWER: nothing fails; shellcheck only.

tasks.title: jq `A + B as $x |` precedence differs on CI jq 1.7.1
tasks.prompt: I am adding a helper to scripts/lib.sh that runs: jq -n --argjson base "$B" --argjson over "$O" '$base + $over as $m | $m.rules | length'. All tests pass on my Windows machine. Is there anything about this jq program that can break in our CI, and how should I check it before pushing? Don't edit any files. End with one line that starts with ANSWER: and gives the corrected jq program and how to verify it.
truth: native project_jq18_vs_ci_jq17_as_precedence.md (PR #105: 45 test-rules-layers failures on ubuntu jq 1.7.1)
code shows only the fixed shape: scripts/lib.sh:3427@497fe05 ") as $effective |", no rationale
tasks.gold_answer:
CI (ubuntu-latest) runs jq 1.7.1, which binds as to the term on its left: $base + ($over as $m | ...), so it adds an object to a number and errors. Local jq 1.8.1 hides it.
ANSWER: use ($base + $over) as $m | $m.rules | length and run the touched tests with a jq 1.7.1 binary shimmed first on PATH.
wrong_answers: ANSWER: the program is fine; nothing to change.
ANSWER: use --arg instead of --argjson; jq 1.6 on CI lacks --argjson.

tasks.title: Windows jq emits CRLF on stdout
tasks.prompt: I am writing a new check under scripts/ that does: while IFS=$'\t' read -r name src; do [ -d "$src" ] || echo "missing $src"; done < <(jq -r '.plugins[] | [.name, .source] | @tsv' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json). On my Windows Git-Bash machine it reports every entry except the last one as missing even though all the directories exist; on Linux it is fine. What is the cause, and what is the fix this repo uses for it? Don't edit any files. End with one line that starts with ANSWER: and gives the cause and the corrected pipeline.
truth: scripts/validate-plugin.sh:99-103@497fe05 (comment + jq ... | tr -d CR)
native project_jq_windows_crlf_stdout.md
tasks.gold_answer:
Windows jq writes stdout in text mode, so every record ends in CRLF; the last field of each non-last record keeps a trailing \r.
ANSWER: cause = jq CRLF output on Windows; fix = jq -r ... marketplace.json | tr -d CR-char (\r) before the while-read loop.
wrong_answers: ANSWER: the directories are relative; cd to the repo root first.
ANSWER: use IFS=, instead of a tab.

tasks.title: Stale-bundle check, and the linked node_modules trap
tasks.prompt: I changed mcp/src/tools/code-map.ts in a second git worktree. To save disk space I made that worktree's mcp/node_modules a directory link to the main checkout's mcp/node_modules. How do I prove the committed mcp/dist bundle is current before I push? Give me the exact commands in order. Don't edit any files. End with one line that starts with ANSWER: and gives the command sequence.
truth: tests/test-bundle-current.sh:1-16@497fe05 (rebuilds each bundle entry, byte-compares; SKIPs when mcp/node_modules/.bin/esbuild is missing)

native project_worktree_node_modules_junction_bundle_drift.md + wiki entities/esbuild-bundle-drift-from-node-modules-junction: a linked node_modules makes esbuild embed resolved sibling-tree paths so the gate fails falsely; remove the link (never rm -rf) and run a real npm ci
tasks.gold_answer:
A linked node_modules makes esbuild embed resolved paths from the other tree, so the bundle differs byte-for-byte.
ANSWER: remove only the link with node fs.unlinkSync on mcp/node_modules (never rm -rf), cd mcp && npm ci && npm run bundle, commit mcp/dist, then bash tests/test-bundle-current.sh.
wrong_answers: ANSWER: cd mcp && npm run bundle && cd .. && bash tests/test-bundle-current.sh
ANSWER: rm -rf mcp/node_modules && cd mcp && npm ci && npm run bundle && bash ../tests/test-bundle-current.sh

tasks.title: Where brain/knowledge dir resolution must live
tasks.prompt: I am adding a new MCP tool under mcp/src/tools/ that writes files into the user knowledge directory. How should it work out that directory so it behaves the same on Windows as on Linux and macOS, and what must I avoid? Don't edit any files. End with one line that starts with ANSWER: and gives the helper to call and the file it lives in.
truth: mcp/src/brain-paths.ts:1-49@497fe05 (resolveKnowledgeDir: plugin option > KNOWLEDGE_DIR > homedir()/knowledge; never process.env.HOME)
mcp/src/brain-paths.test.ts:44@497fe05
tasks.gold_answer:
Node on Windows does not inherit HOME, so a HOME-based join becomes cwd-relative.
ANSWER: call resolveKnowledgeDir() from mcp/src/brain-paths.ts (it uses os.homedir()); never read process.env.HOME.
wrong_answers: ANSWER: path.join(process.env.HOME || "", "knowledge") in the tool file.
ANSWER: read KNOWLEDGE_DIR directly in the tool.

tasks.title: Do not use ln -s for directory links on MSYS
tasks.prompt: I need a new install step that points each plugin version's mcp/node_modules at one shared dependencies directory through a directory link, and it must work on Windows Git-Bash as well as on Linux and macOS. How should the script create that link? Don't edit any files. End with one line that starts with ANSWER: and gives the command to use on each platform.
truth: bin/install-vector-deps.sh:82-90@497fe05 (MINGW/MSYS: node fs.symlinkSync(target, link, junction); else ln -s)
native project_lnstar_windows_deepcopy.md (ln -s silently deep-copies on MSYS)
tasks.gold_answer:
On Git-Bash ln -s silently deep-copies the directory.
ANSWER: MINGW/MSYS: node fs.symlinkSync(target, link, "junction") with cygpath -w paths; Linux/macOS: ln -s target link.
wrong_answers: ANSWER: ln -s "$SHARED" mcp/node_modules on all platforms.
ANSWER: export MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict and use ln -s everywhere.

tasks.title: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV contaminates tests/run-all.sh
tasks.prompt: On my Windows Git-Bash machine, bash tests/run-all.sh suddenly shows about a dozen red tests, several of them claiming a file does not exist when it clearly does. CI on the same commit is green and I have not changed any code since my last green local run. What is the most likely cause in my shell environment, and what should I do before re-running? Don't edit any files. End with one line that starts with ANSWER: and gives the cause and the command to run first.
truth: docs/daily-prompt.md:405-412@497fe05 (export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 turned 12 of 17 tests red; unset -> green)

surfaces.repo_skills: one chronicle mention of a different incident

tasks.gold_answer:
An exported MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 stops Git-Bash path conversion, so tests hand POSIX paths to Windows tools that cannot open them.
ANSWER: cause = MSYS_NO_PATHCONV exported in the shell; run unset MSYS_NO_PATHCONV, then re-run one failing test before the suite.
wrong_answers: ANSWER: CRLF line endings from core.autocrlf; run git add --renormalize .
ANSWER: flaky timeouts; re-run the suite.
